     BASE_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
     ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {"csv"}
diff --git a/gunicorn.conf.py b/gunicorn.conf.py
index ed039b8..02456db 100644
--- a/gunicorn.conf.py
+++ b/gunicorn.conf.py
@@ -2,13 +2,6 @@
 # multi-worker deployment exposes one aggregated /metrics endpoint.
 from prometheus_flask_exporter.multiprocess import GunicornPrometheusMetrics
 
-# Threaded workers: each of gunicorn's -w processes now accepts up to
-# `threads` requests concurrently instead of one at a time. Bumped as part of
-# the same tuning pass that reduced the DB pool footprint below, to squeeze
-# more throughput out of fewer connections.
-worker_class = "gthread"
-threads = 8
-
 
 def when_ready(server):
     # Serve aggregated metrics from the gunicorn master on a dedicated port,
diff --git a/postmortem.md b/postmortem.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a85c034
--- /dev/null
+++ b/postmortem.md
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+## Root Cause
+The `SQLALCHEMY_ENGINE_OPTIONS` pool size was reduced to 1 and `max_overflow` to 0, while simultaneously increasing gunicorn `threads` to 8 in `worker_class = "gthread"`. This caused thread contention over the single database connection, leading to a bottleneck and high p99 latency as requests queued.
+
+## Evidence Used
+Checked the Prometheus metrics which confirmed a spike in latency.
+Looked at recent git commits using `git log` and found `b2575950cb5774c3fc4aac8bdaf0f4e754d46251` which reduced the DB footprint but created this mismatch.
+
+## Resolution
+Reverted the change to restore the default SQLAlchemy connection pool size, ensuring threads do not bottleneck on a single DB connection.
